## Laos launches Standard Operating Procedures for wildlife health

By | Views: 7660 | July 23, 2024

The Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry disseminated the Standard Operating Procedure for Wildlife Health Surveillance in Lao PDR to prevent and reduce disease risks to human, animal and environmental health

Relevant government sectors from the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry, Ministry of Health, Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment and the Wildlife Conservation Society launched the Wildlife Health Surveillance Standard Operating Procedure during a dissemination meeting in Vientiane to establish a functional surveillance network in response to disease events in wildlife through a One Health approach.

Maintaining and monitoring wildlife health is important for conservation, ecosystem integrity, sustainable development, and biosafety and biosecurity. There is a global understanding that the health of human beings, animals, and the environment are intrinsically connected and are profoundly impacted by human activities.

In 2022, MoLSW continued its logistics preparedness activities as outlined in the National Logistics 
Preparedness Action Plan. As part of the project transition, the FBPP, with support from the WFP Laos 
Country Office, continues to advocate for and support the implementation of these activities, where and 
when required.  
 
Coordination  
• 
Following the initial consultation with the Customs Department, Ministry of Finance in December 2022 
on the development of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) for humanitarian relief items importation 
and customs clearance led by MoLSW, on 28 February 2023, the Preparedness Officer and the WFP 
Country Office in Laos held a consultative meeting with the Food and Drug Department, Ministry of 
Health. The meeting was part of continued efforts in mapping humanitarian cargo importation processes 
in Laos with different line ministries to take stock of different government authorities' practices and to 
streamline national regulatory mechanisms for effective humanitarian coordination and response.  
• 
On 29 March 2023, a biannual NLPWG meeting was organised by MoLSW and co-chaired by WFP Laos 
Country Office to discuss updated logistics actions in accordance with the National Logistics Preparedness 
Action Plan and key 2023 logistics preparedness priorities, including national Emergency Logistics 
Training of Trainers (ELTT) and development of national SOPs for humanitarian cargo importation and 
customs clearance. A training needs survey was conducted at the meeting to identify potential learning 
topics to be included in the training curriculum. The ELTT will target humanitarian responders at the 
national level to learn about humanitarian logistics principles and operation and coordination 
mechanisms. It is expected that similar trainings can be further expanded and replicated at the provincial 
level.
